notes: 2026-11-15: size_threshold_bytes lowered from 16777216 (16 MiB) to 4194304 (4 MiB) to match the code change in internal/usecase/splitfile.go (maxSplitPartSize) and internal/usecase/markitdown.go (maxFileSize), committed as 'feat: reduce maximum file size limit from 16MB to 4MB'. size_class below was recomputed against the NEW threshold by `go run ./loadtest/tools/verifyfixtures -write` (re-fetches/re-hashes every object; bytes/sha256 were unchanged, only size_class flipped for fixtures between 4 MiB and the old 16 MiB line). Every expected_parts value computed under the OLD 16 MiB part-size budget was invalidated by this change (a smaller max part size changes how many parts every large-splitter format produces) and was reset to null except where re-verified by an actual smoke run under the new code -- see per-fixture notes for which ones that is.

Each fixture needs its own real bytes/sha256 measured against the actual object in MinIO -- never a single shared size for every file, and never a part count inferred from bytes (structural splitting + re-encoding can change the effective size).

size_class is derived from the ACTUAL byte count vs size_threshold_bytes (4 MiB, the SplitFile/ConvertURLToMarkdownFile threshold in internal/usecase/{splitfile,markitdown}.go): 'small' means the original URL is returned unsplit; 'large' means the Splitter fans it out into parts no larger than 4 MiB each.

All 15 fixtures below are `verified: true`: every bytes/sha256/size_class value was freshly re-fetched, re-hashed and re-classified against the live MinIO 'dataset' bucket (deploy/docker-compose.test.yaml, localhost:19000) via `go run ./loadtest/tools/verifyfixtures -write` on verified_at. The six small PDF/DOCX/XLSX fixtures, the original boundary CSVs and the new 4 MiB boundary CSVs were generated with real, varied content (not padding) and uploaded via `go run ./loadtest/tools/seedfixtures`; re-run both if the underlying MinIO data is ever reset.

If a future entry is added as a placeholder (object not uploaded yet), mark it `verified: false` with null bytes/sha256 -- k6/load_test.js refuses unverified fixtures by default (ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_FIXTURES=false) specifically so a capacity run never silently rests on unconfirmed data.

expected_parts is 1 for every size_class=small fixture: that is a direct contract guarantee (SplitFile returns the original URL as the sole part whenever the real file is within size_threshold_bytes), not an inference about how a large file would be cut.

expected_parts is left null for every size_class=large fixture until it has actually been observed under the CURRENT code+threshold: publish that single fixture once, read the resulting SUCCESS event on stream:doc-extractor:output, and copy its `total` field here. Do not compute it from ceil(bytes / 4MiB).

url is the MinIO address reachable from INSIDE the docker-compose network (what gets embedded in the input event's file_path, since the Splitter/Extractor containers fetch it, not the k6 host). url_host is the same object reachable from the host (e.g. via deploy/docker-compose.test.yaml's published MinIO port), for the verifyfixtures tool and for manual smoke checks.

Two formats flagged 'synthetic padding' below (see docs/load-test-review-event-sourcing.md P2) are generated with comment-padding (PDF) or ZIP_STORED, uncompressed, low-structure content (DOCX/XLSX): their physical byte count is real, but they may not represent the CPU/memory cost of extracting an equivalent real-world document. Treat them as one data point, not a stand-in for all real documents of that size.

pdf-small-8mib keeps its original id even though it is now size_class=large under the 4 MiB threshold: it is the PDF that timed out at 120s under the OLD 16 MiB threshold (run-002, docs/load-test-results-event-sourcing.md), so it is the regression case for whether lowering the threshold to 4 MiB avoids this timeout by splitting the file instead of passing it through whole. Do not reclassify it away from this role.

fixtures.notes: Generated by tmp/generate_ultrasmall.py (real, varied sentence content, not padding), ~85 KiB target, 92,386 bytes actual -- strictly <= 100,000 bytes, unlike docx-small-100kb/xlsx-small-100kb which are ~104-110KB (slightly over 100KB despite the name). Kept for reference/regression history; do not use as the default ultra-small fixture going forward.

Generated by tmp/generate_real_fixtures.py: randomized real sentences (not padding), ~8 MiB. Was size_class=small (pass-through, no split) and timed out at 120s under the OLD 16 MiB threshold (run-002). Now size_class=large under the 4 MiB threshold, so the Splitter cuts it into multiple ~4 MiB page-span parts instead of passing it through whole -- this is the regression case for whether that avoids the timeout. See top-level notes. Smoke-verified 2026-11-15 under the current 4 MiB threshold/code: the Splitter does cut it into 3 parts (confirmed via the real SUCCESS/FAILED state's `total` field), but terminal outcome is FAILED, not SUCCESS -- 2 of the 3 parts still individually exceed the 120s convert_timeout (markitdown killed by SIGKILL after 120.0s each). Splitting by average page-byte-size does not bound a single dense page's own conversion cost; this regression is NOT resolved by the threshold change alone. Keep reporting this as a known unresolved regression, not as sizing data.
